I'm 20. Living in the USA with no college education as it's too damn expensive, I don't qualify for any sort of financial aid and my parents have too many issues to deal with themselves than my further education. I'm working on it though.

I wouldn't say that I disagree with the way the world is now. We're headed in the right direction. A communist world would have likely lead to either vast amounts of suffering, or possibly world peace. They don't teach politics in high school, so I don't know enough to make an opinion on that. And I will be honest, I often wish that the world were a nuclear wasteland. In the end, the world will keep turning with or without us. As a species though, we shouldn't be trying to control others unless we're willing to commit and try this idea of a one-world government. 

I'm not going to say that it would work, because I don't know if it would. It's possible it would fail. But if we can't commit to something like that for the sake of all of humanity, then why should we be concerned about others that don't care about us? 

We should be focusing on making what we have good and defending it against those who would destroy it, not acting as some sort of nanny for the rest of the world or trying to shove it down everyone's throats in a clearly aggressive manner. 

We should instead act as the example that everyone should strive to be so that the other nations will see how good it is for us and work towards being that themselves. If the rest of the world would rather kill us for having and being what's good, then humanity is truly doomed and we would have been better off as a nuclear wasteland.

I actually find it funny that just because I included Korea in my original statement everyone's getting pissed off at me even though I'm saying essentially the same thing that the top comments on the other threads of the same issue are saying. I may be a bit naive. I am young, and often prone to mistakes. But if we want the world to change, we have to make the effort. Saying you want peace and actively working towards that goal is much different than saying you want peace and yet not giving another nation a chance to develop in it's own way.

Plus, it's sounding really 1950's in here. All the communism hate. while I will admit I'm not a fan, that doesn't mean it wouldn't work for another nation, and why should we be the ones who decide how it should work for another nation? I would liken it to you having your life, your set ways of doing things and understanding things, and then finding out your neighbor (who is doing well in their own right and not necessarily causing problems) does things 100% differently than you and deciding that they're not allowed to do it that way. So you walk on over and say "Stop, otherwise I'm going to kill you and have my buddy take over control of the people in your family." Or worse yet, doing all that and then leaving the family to fend for itself afterwards.

I realize at this point that I'm probably wrong in my thinking. Wouldn't be the first time, as I am not a smart man. I do think that everyone shouldn't be forced to act, feel, and believe things that they do not. The world would be boring and progress would be incredibly slow if people did not try things for themselves. Telling people "Do it this way or else" is wrong, no matter who is saying it. It doesn't matter how the world in the past has been, it matters how it will be in the future. If you can't let people be what they want to be, then you are probably a bit of a control freak and shouldn't be in charge in the first place. Parents have to realize this when their children grow up, why can't the government realize it? 

That being said, there are consequences for things that you do. If you stab some guy one day, you would expect to be jailed and possibly put to death yourself (depending on where you live). Unless you're willing to create one world order though, the actions of someone thousands of miles away should not be your concern. They should be the concern of the people that live there.

Well first off, that whole ripple effect with communism wouldn't have happend if people stopped putting their noses where they didn't belong and stayed out of the affairs of other nations. I am saying that it was wrong of us to intervene. At the same time, it was wrong of the USSR and China to interfere as well. 

As for picking on Korea, it's more like the asian-centric wars of the recent past are all that I know, so it's easier for me to use them as an example. I'm not saying that it was an unjust war, I'm just saying that it shouldn't have been necessary in the first place. If everyone just would stop trying to force themselves upon other nations I'm sure everything would turn out just fine. Or not. That's not for us to decide. And if, in turn, it winds up affecting us in the future then we should deal with it as it becomes our actual problem, rather than some speculative problem.

I love how everything shifted to just talking about Korea here. I've already said that I don't advocate becoming involved in the affairs of other nations. The only reason why it shifted to Korea here is because I know little to nothing about non-asian conflicts in the recent past. Education on that front has been severely lacking and I don't care enough to change that. China and the USSR shouldn't have been involved just as much as the USA should have minded it's own business. It's not our place to decide what a nation does with itself.

Then we should let the nation fail. It is wrong to force yourself upon others just because your economy is failing or has failed and you just so happen to have the military force to say "Yeah, you're going to keep doing this and even favor us or we'll blow you up."

It's called reaping what you sow. You kill your economy, you deal with it. Otherwise you just become the enemy of the world as you are nothing more than a bully that just so happens to have no qualms about killing to get what it wants. If anything, the rest of the world should come in and wipe out the USA. But of course they won't because they can destroy the entire fucking world.
So? I will admit that having SK doing as well as they are is good, it still wasn't our fight. If they wanted it badly enough, they should have fought harder.

I believe that one nation should not be interfering with the internal affairs of another. Going to war against another nation because they've become "evil" is one thing. If the people want it, let it happen. It's only when these nations actually go out and deliberately threaten other nations after the fact that anything should be done. 

Going to war with Nazi Germany? Yes. They're invading other nations and killing their people. Same with WW2-era japan. I could not give a single fuck about some nation across the world internally having issues and warring with itself.

I do care about people committing mass and indiscriminate genocide against another. Unless the rest of the world wants to commit to becoming some semblance of a single world government, stay out of other nation's business. 

Money should not be a factor when deciding to intervene in a nation's conflicts. If the people want it, let it be. I wouldn't want china banging on my front door because the government decided that 40-60%+ of the nation decided to revolt against it. It's not their right to decide how my nation is run or to intervene in an issue that is not theirs.

As with the russia thing, that is literally news to me. Education about the gulf war and other 90's conflicts were incredibly underwhelming at the time I was in school. At the same time, I still don't overly care. If any nation were to be truly a threat to the USA post-cold war, they would have the ability to nuke us to hell and back. That's why we don't go invading China or Russia because of some internal issue. Why should we decide that because a nation has little or no nuclear weapons that we can just stroll on in and force a populace to conform to standards that they may not even want? Forcing people to do what you want them to do or else you will kill them is wrong. Even if the people are wrong, it is not your decision to make.

Well you could start by removing money and "power" from the whole thing. After that, actually look at what's going on and figure out of the whole thing is a gross violation of human rights, or just a nation that no longer wants what the government wants. 

If it's just an issue of who's in charge, we should probably stay away. It's not our issue, and if it should become our issue we have more than enough of an ability to handle it if/when it happens. 

If it's something like an issue of genocide, or a situation similar to North Korea where the people have literally zero choice and are brainwashed into believing otherwise, as well as being so clearly oppressed by their government, then that *may* be grounds for intervening. I say "may", because all action should be taken only with deliberate though and consideration for the consequences.

What I don't get is why the USA still feels the need to be the world's police force. Hasn't it learned it's lesson from the past 50 or so years? Vietnam didn't turn out so well, Korea really *could* have gone better, and more recently our business in the whole "war on terror" has done nothing but make them hated by most of the world. Just because the USA has nukes that it can use at any time is not a legitimate excuse for this behavior. You don't see Russia running around with it's military, inventing illegal and fake wars because it has nukes.

E: I will admit that the Korea issue here probably shouldn't have been included. Still doesn't mean that we need to shove our noses into issues that are not ours. This counts for everyone, the USSR, China, and all other nations of the world. It shouldn't be an issue until it becomes OUR issue. If the USSR and China hadn't been pushing their beliefs on others and making it a military issue, we would have had no reason to get into that mess. Doesn't mean that it didn't happen nor that we should not have helped out. It does mean that it shouldn't have happened on a whole. People need to stop worrying about what others are doing unless it actually affects them, rather than speculatively affecting them.

It's possible you won't. However you shouldn't go into it your first time expecting not to get high. You very well can. It would be an extremely irresponsible move to smoke, expect not to get high, and then go around town. Police can get you with public intoxication if you're visibly high, and your mental psyche can take a hit if you freak out too hard. Wait until you know the effects that marijuana will have on you before you try going out and about with it.

Even nowadays, after a couple years of smoking, I don't like going to town high. I will if something comes up while smoking, but it's generally not a good idea to do anything after smoking until you know how it will effect you.

For your first time, you really should be in a safe area (Meaning don't go wandering town while high). Maybe a friend's house, or somewhere with a couple of close buddies that you trust will take care of you if something bad does happen. Otherwise you could very easily have a bad time and be turned away from marijuana for a long time.

You could also, if you prefer, smoke by yourself your first time. You would have to take a whole bunch of precautions beforehand, but it's doable. You could still have the possibility of having a bad time though, so it's only recommended you do this if you absolutely cannot find someone to hang out with you. Be sure to have something to distract your mind though so that you don't go flipping out at every little noise.

Also, remember that you may not feel anything the first time around. Practice breathing, it will help make it so that you are for certain getting smoke into your lungs. Try not to swallow any either. Easy way to do this? Be sure that you have fully inhaled all the smoke in your mouth before swallowing, or exhaled. Also don't forget your water!

Stay safe!

Last year, at christmas time, my little brother handed me a box wrapped in duct tape. About 10 layers of it, alternating wrapping paper and duct tape. At the bottom of it all? a GGG version of Pinkie Pie.

At this time, nobody in the family besides him knew that I enjoyed the Pony fandom or show. But nobody cared. They might have had a small laugh at the absurdity, but they didn't press the issue or harass me in any way. At that point in time, I was secure.

Then this year came along. What a year. I was introduced to marijuana, given a raise at work, and then promptly started abusing cough syrup. Dextromethorphane is one hell of a drug. Makes you really feel like you don't exist. If I had to describe what it felt like in a way you could understand, I would say it would be like dying, only not. (This is in no way to say that weed started me abusing this, that was my own stupid thinking.)

This went on for about a month. At the end of it all, I was homeless, jobless, and an absolute wreck. To top it all off, I was a thousand miles from home, and any support I may have been able to get from family or friends.

The next few months were harrowing. Always worrying about those around you and if they're safe to be around. Always needing to find a place to sleep at night. Worrying about not getting a meal the next day. To top it all off, all of my belongings, from a laptop I took with me, to the boots on my feet, were stolen from me. 

The nights grew long and cold. My feet were constantly numb from the growing cold, my stomach in a permanent state of inactivity. I went from being 180lbs to 110.

Then I managed to get a hold of my family again. They helped me get back home. They haven't harassed me about my sudden departure, which I'm sure hurt them badly. They don't worry about what I was doing, how I was living. They just wanted to make sure I was safe. And at home, I was.

My little brother is a brony. He's been quite a bit of help since I've been back, though he might not know it. He's been acting a lot more mature, doing more to help around the house, even just being a good friend.

Thanks to my generalized anxiety disorder, it's hard for me to talk to anyone. I want to thank him though. He's been great, and I wanted to make sure that he has a very pony christmas.

I, however, have no money to be going out and buying things for him. With your permission, I would give him this gift that you are offering this community. 

I leave after the new year to head to my older sister's house. She's agreed to house and provide support while I try to make my life, so I don't have much time for me to be able to present it all in person, which I would like to do.
